_schema: The unit roster dictionary (Rival-authored, 2026-08-07, per the military design session). Each row is a UNIT TYPE a nation can field: {era_band, unit_class (combat.hpp enum), type_power_mod (per-mille, layered on the class matchup), doctrine_options (named doctrine_row presets this type may fight under), available_when (the DERIVATION of availability — endowment classes + industrialisation year from settlement_state, never research or player choice), named_substitutions (stand-in signals, flagged per the BL-221 convention)}. This is the NOUN half of the unit dictionary; the VERB half is BL-314 (unit verb family), filed design-owed with its transcription debt named.
_note: Sibling of ACTIONS.json (verbs) on the noun axis: its natural Io analogue is the recipe/building-type registry, not the action dictionary. unit_component.type's opaque uint16_t is the index into this table when it lands.

Era-keying lives HERE and only here (Ben, 2026-08-07): verbs stay era-invariant; a single verb precondition points at this table's derivation. combat.hpp is era-blind by contract and resolve_battle takes fully-resolved stacks, so nothing in this file leaks into the engine.

Availability is DERIVED, not unlocked: a nation's available rows are a pure function of its provinces' endowment classes and its industrialisation year (both already in settlement_state, BL-273/BL-218). No research, no unlock events. The forge-god culture fields iron early; the late industrialiser fields pike against rifles. (BL-274's filing position, ratified.)

Four era bands (decision taken 2026-08-07, lean ratified by session): classical / medieval-equivalent / gunpowder / industrial. The 1960 campaign era is just the last rows of the same table — BL-272's engine-parity contract made concrete.
Unit-type names are generic mechanism nouns (levy foot, horse raiders, pike block), never Earth proper nouns, per the standing naming rule. Doctrine preset names likewise.

NAVAL rows are strategic-only: combat.hpp gives naval zero tactical power. They exist so crossings and blockades have a noun; no naval battle verb exists (honest first cut — flagged, since players and agents will expect one).

Landing path: Rival design artifact, lands into Io explicitly with BL-274 (era-keyed rosters), never by silent merge. type_power_mod values are authored by judgement and calibrate against BL-271 sweep evidence when the sim runs.
Position/grain contract (session rulings, 2026-08-07): units sit on a TILE (BL-157 stands; the shipped unit_component's body field is the divergence to fix at landing), and verbs act at UNIT grain.

shield_wall.note: Devastating frontal, brittle flank, poor in mountains — the close-order block.

storm.note: Take the walls now, pay in blood.

massed_volley.note: Gunpowder line discipline: murderous frontal arcs, exposed flanks.

levy_foot.note: The floor: any province with population fields these. Manpower cost only.

named_substitutions.copper_and_tin: single ore_q axis stands in for the two-metal trade signal — flagged

bronze_spear_block.note: Close-order metal-armed foot; the first endowment-gated row.

iron_line.note: The forge-god row: iron early is the classical band's decisive asymmetry.

named_substitutions.horses: grassland share of the province window stands in for a pasture/domesticable-clade axis that does not exist — flagged (BL-274 open question 2, resolved as this substitution)

horse_raiders.note: Horse-country's answer to the shield wall.

named_substitutions.bow_staves: forest share stands in for a bow-wood signal — flagged

rams_and_towers.note: The classical siege train; slow, exists to make walls answerable.

war_galleys.note: Strategic-only: carries crossings and blockades, zero tactical power.

armoured_lancers.note: Horse country plus iron country in one polity: the medieval band's apex.

pike_block.note: The lancer's answer; holds the gunpowder transition's losing side.

named_substitutions.saltpetre_and_sulphur: energy class stands in for a dedicated saltpetre/sulphur signal — flagged (BL-274's filing substitution, ratified)

matchlock_foot.note: The band-breaker: pike loses to this, and diffusion along contact decides who has it (BL-271 sim mechanic, per BL-274 open question 3's lean).

field_bombards.note: Walls stop mattering; the medieval defensive equilibrium ends here.

rifle_line.note: Gated on the Stage 4 furnace date alone: the first industrialiser fields these against pike, which is the philosophical-development instrument in one row.

steam_squadrons.note: Strategic-only. The 1960 campaign navy is later rows of this same column.
